questions.question: What is intercultural competence?
options: The ability to communicate effectively across cultures
Fluency in at least five languages
questions.explanation: Intercultural competence is the ability to communicate effectively and appropriately across cultural differences.

questions.question: What is ethnocentrism?
options: Judging other cultures by the standards of your own
questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism means measuring other cultures against your own as the norm — the opposite of cultural relativism.

questions.question: What is cultural relativism?
options: Understanding cultures on their own terms
Ranking cultures from best to worst
questions.explanation: Cultural relativism seeks to understand practices within their own cultural context rather than judging by outside standards.

questions.question: Which areas commonly differ between cultures?
options: Communication styles, concepts of time, personal space and formality
questions.explanation: Key differences include direct vs. indirect communication, time and punctuality, personal space, hierarchy and humor.

questions.question: A Dutch colleague gives very direct criticism that a Japanese colleague finds rude. What explains this?
options: Different cultural norms for direct versus indirect communication
The Dutch colleague is simply impolite
questions.explanation: Directness norms vary culturally: what is honest feedback in one culture can seem rude in another.
